task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of September 1, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style newspaper news update about Wayfern Transfer's lower cash-transfer fee and what changes, and does not change, in the recipient's payment.

facts.text: Wayfern Transfer announced Tuesday, Sept. 1, 2026, that its fee on qualifying transfers to fictional Keldra will fall from $4 to $2 on Sept. 15.
The change applies when a customer sends $100 through $500, inclusive, in a cash-funded transfer at one of eight local agency counters; the amount range excludes the separate fee.
Transfers through a different online product retain their own fee schedule.
The transfer fee is charged in addition to the amount sent, rather than deducted from that amount.
Wayfern's currency-conversion margin is unchanged by the announcement.
For the supplied Sept. 1 quote, the reference exchange rate was 10 Keldran luma per dollar and Wayfern offered 9.8.
Holding the September 1 exchange quote constant, a $200 transfer would pay 1,960 luma to the recipient and cost the sender $202 with the new fee, compared with $204 under the current fee.
The quoted exchange rate is a dated example and is not guaranteed to remain available on Sept. 15 or later.
The company says recipients pay no additional Wayfern collection fee through the payout partners covered by this offer; the packet does not name those partners.
The record does not establish charges imposed by unrelated banks or intermediaries outside those partners.
Wayfern processed 12,400 transfers on this route last month, a transaction count rather than a count of different senders.
Manager Iona Pell said a renegotiated agency contract made the lower fee possible; its commercial terms were not disclosed.
Customer Reni Moss sends money for a relative's household expenses and uses a counter because she prefers a printed receipt.
Moss said, "The fee on my side matters, but I also ask what number appears on the other side."
Pell said, "The transfer fee is lower. We are not saying every part of the exchange has become cheaper."
The company will display the amount paid and the payout amount before a customer confirms a transfer.
Expected payout timing remains the next business day, subject to the existing identity and transaction checks.
The announcement contains no end date for the lower fee but does not lock future exchange rates or all future fees.
Wayfern opened its first local counter in a travel shop in 2010.
The reporting packet supplies no market-wide ranking proving Wayfern is the cheapest provider.

forbidden_additions: All transfer costs are halved or the dated exchange rate is guaranteed
A cheapest-provider ranking or no charges anywhere beyond the covered payout partners
